title: U.S. House · Virginia's 3rd District
area: Virginia's 3rd Congressional District (Newport News, Hampton, Portsmouth, and part of Norfolk)

context.text: Both primaries were canceled. Incumbent Robert C. "Bobby" Scott advanced unopposed as the Democratic nominee, and Edwin Rivera advanced unopposed as the Republican nominee.

summary.text: Robert C. "Bobby" Scott is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for Virginia's 3rd District, in office since 1993. A Newport News attorney by training, he served in the Virginia House of Delegates and Virginia Senate before Congress and is the ranking member of the House Education and Workforce Committee.

background.text: Born in Washington, D.C. in 1947 and grew up in Newport News, Virginia; graduated from Groton School in 1965.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Harvard University in 1969 and a J.D. from Boston College School of Law in 1973.
Served in the U.S. Army Reserve (1970-1974) and the Massachusetts National Guard (1974-1976).
Worked as an attorney in private practice in Newport News from 1973 to 1991.
Elected to the Virginia House of Delegates in 1977, serving until 1983, then to the Virginia Senate, serving until 1993.
Lost his first race for Congress in 1986, in the 1st District, to Republican incumbent Herb Bateman, 56% to 44%.

Elected to the U.S. House in 1992 from the newly created 3rd District and has served since 1993; Wikipedia describes him as the first African American representative from Virginia since Reconstruction and the dean of Virginia's congressional delegation.
Serves on the House Committee on Education and the Workforce, where he is the ranking member; Democratic colleagues elected him ranking member in December 2022.

positions.summary: As vice-chair of the House Democratic Caucus Gun Violence Prevention Task Force, lists reinstating a federal assault weapons ban among the Task Force’s recommendations to Congress, alongside strengthening the background check database.
positions.quote: Reinstate and strengthen a prospective federal ban on assault weapons.

positions.summary: His official site says he strongly supports maintaining and strengthening Medicare and Medicaid, opposes efforts to weaken or repeal the Affordable Care Act, and describes himself as a strong supporter of single-payer health care.
positions.quote: Congressman Scott strongly supports maintaining and strengthening these programs to make sure that those who need them most can continue to rely on them.

positions.summary: His official site says he supports the Green New Deal, has cosponsored renewable-energy investment legislation, and has opposed opening new areas off Virginia’s coast to offshore oil and gas development.
positions.quote: Scott has co-sponsored legislation in the House of Representatives that would promote investment in renewable energy, and is a supporter of the Green New Deal.

positions.summary: In an April 2, 2025 statement, said the across-the-board tariffs announced by President Trump would raise costs on Americans.
positions.quote: President Trump’s across-the-board tariffs are reckless and will raise costs on Americans without making the long overdue investments in American manufacturing capacity that would create jobs.

positions.summary: In January 2026, joined a letter from Virginia House Democrats to DHS and ICE opposing a proposed ICE processing facility in Hanover County and a potential 10,000-bed detention center in Stafford County.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Education and the Workforce and the House Committee on Budget in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Chaired the House Committee on Education and the Workforce in the 116th and 117th Congresses (2019-2023), when Democrats held the House majority.

summary.text: Edwin Rivera is the Republican nominee for Virginia's 3rd District. According to Ballotpedia, he grew up in Puerto Rico, lives in Newport News, served in the U.S. Army, and has worked as a police officer. His campaign website lists education reform, public safety, and opposing tolls on the Hampton Roads Bridge-Tunnel among his priorities.

background.text: Grew up in Puerto Rico and lives in Newport News, Virginia.
Served in the U.S. Army and has worked as a police officer.
Became the Republican nominee without appearing on a primary ballot, after the August 4, 2026 Republican primary was canceled.

priorities.text: Campaigns on education reform, including raising teacher pay, renovating failing schools, and supporting HBCU funding and career/technical pathways.
Opposes tolls on the Hampton Roads Bridge-Tunnel and supports capping tolls.
Supports expanded veterans' benefits, including preventive healthcare for veterans with two or more enlistments and full Tricare Prime coverage during wartime for National Guard/Reserve members.

positions.summary: His campaign platform says to increase and fully fund law enforcement and community-based programs.
positions.quote: Increase and support(fully fund) law enforcement and community based programs (such as national night out) which helps strengthen relationships across our different communities.

summary.text: Makiba Gaines is an independent candidate for Virginia's 3rd District. She describes herself as a practicing civil rights attorney in solo practice and a Christian, wife, and mother, and is based in the Chesapeake area. Her campaign website says she is running to make life more affordable and to protect peace, stability, and prosperity.

background.text: According to her BallotReady profile, earned an associate's degree in English and bachelor's degrees in political science and in law from Penn State University, and a J.D. from Regent University.
BallotReady lists her as an attorney at Polaris Law Firm since 2021 and, in 2021, litigation counsel at the Buried Alive Project.

According to her campaign website, she is a practicing civil rights attorney who has represented children and other vulnerable groups in federal and state courts and has worked to free people from federal prison; she says she has litigated against corporations and government officials as a solo practitioner.

priorities.text: Says she is running to make life more affordable, protect peace and stability, and ensure collective prosperity.
priorities.quote: Send me to Congress to make your life more affordable, to protect your peace and stability, and to help ensure our collective prosperity.

summary.text: Stephen "Steve" Woll is an independent candidate for Virginia's 3rd District. According to his campaign website, he is a Navy veteran, scientist, and businessman who grew up in Pittsburgh and has lived in Hampton Roads for more than 25 years. He says he is running as a representative who answers to the district rather than to a party.

background.text: According to his campaign website, grew up in Pittsburgh and lived in several places before the Navy brought him to Hampton Roads more than 25 years ago.

Says he attended Officer Candidate School and served 21 years in the Navy as a Meteorology and Oceanography Officer, including aboard the USS Harry S. Truman on September 11, a deployment supporting Operation Iraqi Freedom, and a final assignment commanding support operations for a dozen aircraft carriers and large-deck amphibious ships across the Atlantic Fleet.

After leaving the Navy, says he worked in the private sector helping companies and clients use data, technology, and teamwork on operational problems, including public-private partnerships in Hampton Roads, and has for several years worked with a veteran-inspired service organization focused on civic divides.

researchNotes: No biography, campaign website, or public statements were found for independent candidates Makiba Gaines or Stephen Woll within the research budget, so their entries are minimal. Edwin Rivera's campaign site (edwinriveraforcongress.com) returned a 403 bot challenge and could not be read; his entry is unchanged. Makiba Gaines's site states general priorities but no positions on the guide's issues. Makiba Gaines's and Stephen Woll's biographies come from their own campaign materials and, for Gaines, a BallotReady profile; they are self-described, and no independent news profile was found for either. Edwin Rivera's biography rests on Ballotpedia only because his campaign website could not be loaded.
